questions.stem:
Problem: Many students are failing in mathematics in a school.
Course of Action:
I. The school should organise extra coaching classes for weaker students.
II. The school should expel all failing students.
III. The school should review the mathematics curriculum and teaching methods.

options.option_text: Only I follows (wrong: III is also practical and appropriate)
Only II follows (wrong: expelling students doesn't solve the problem)
I and III follow (correct: extra coaching (I) addresses individual students; curriculum review (III) addresses systemic issues; expulsion (II) is extreme and counterproductive ✓)
All three follow (wrong: II is not a constructive course of action)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Course of Action evaluation: (I) Extra coaching = practical, directly helps weak students. (II) Expelling students = extreme, doesn't solve the educational problem and is counterproductive. (III) Reviewing curriculum/teaching = addresses root cause. I and III are both valid remedial actions; II is not.

questions.stem:
Problem: A city has been experiencing severe traffic jams during peak hours.
Course of Action:
I. The government should widen the main roads.
II. The government should promote carpooling and public transport use.
III. All private vehicles should be permanently banned from the city.

options.option_text: Only I follows (wrong: II is also a valid course of action)
Only III follows (wrong: permanent ban is extreme and impractical)
I and II follow (correct: widening roads (I) and promoting alternatives (II) are practical solutions; permanent ban (III) is too extreme ✓)
All three follow (wrong: III is extreme and impractical)

questions.explanation: C is correct. (I) Widening roads = practical infrastructure solution. (II) Promoting carpooling/public transport = reduces vehicle numbers sustainably. (III) Permanent ban = extreme, impractical, would cause economic disruption. I and II are balanced, proportionate actions.

questions.stem:
Problem: There is a shortage of water supply in several areas of the city.
Course of Action:
I. Authorities should repair leaking pipes and reduce wastage.
II. The government should explore rainwater harvesting and water recycling.
III. All residents should be fined heavily for any water use.

options.option_text: Only I follows (wrong: II is also practical)
I and II follow (correct: repairing leaks (I) reduces waste; rainwater harvesting (II) increases supply; fining all residents (III) is extreme ✓)
All three follow (wrong: III punishes normal use, not just waste)
Only III follows (wrong: punishing all residents doesn't increase water supply)

questions.explanation: B is correct. (I) Repairing leaks = directly addresses one cause of shortage (wastage in distribution). (II) Rainwater harvesting/recycling = increases available water supply. (III) Fining all water use = extreme; penalises essential use, not just wasteful use. I and II are constructive.

questions.stem:
Problem: The number of road accidents has increased significantly in recent years.
Course of Action:
I. Strict enforcement of traffic rules and speed limits should be implemented.
II. Road safety education should be included in school curricula.
III. All driving licences should be revoked until accidents decrease.

options.option_text: Only I follows (wrong: II also addresses the root cause through education)
I and II follow (correct: enforcement (I) addresses immediate rule-breaking; education (II) addresses long-term awareness; revoking all licences (III) is extreme ✓)
Only III follows (wrong: revoking all licences would cripple transportation)
All three follow (wrong: III is impractical and extreme)

questions.explanation: B is correct. (I) Stricter enforcement = addresses immediate bad driving behaviour. (II) Education in schools = long-term prevention by building awareness from youth. (III) Revoking ALL licences = extreme, impractical, would prevent essential travel for all citizens. I and II follow.

questions.stem:
Problem: A factory has been found releasing toxic effluents into a nearby river.
Course of Action:
I. The factory should be closed immediately.
II. The factory should install proper waste treatment facilities before resuming operations.
III. The factory management should be educated about environmental regulations.

options.option_text: Only I follows (wrong: a complete permanent closure may be excessive; II addresses root cause)
Only II follows (wrong: II requires time; factory should be stopped immediately while treatment is installed)
I and II follow (correct: immediate closure (I) stops ongoing pollution; requiring treatment facilities (II) before reopening addresses root cause ✓)
All three follow (wrong: education alone (III) is insufficient for an active polluter; I and II are the priority actions)

questions.explanation: C is correct. (I) Immediate closure = necessary to stop active ongoing pollution, which is an emergency. (II) Installing treatment facilities before reopening = long-term solution. (III) Education = too mild for a factory actively polluting; education is for prevention, not cure. I and II are the priority responses.

questions.stem:
Problem: The rate of unemployment among youth has risen sharply.
Course of Action:
I. The government should invest more in vocational training and skill development programmes.
II. The government should create more job opportunities through infrastructure projects.
III. Youth who remain unemployed for more than 6 months should be penalised.

options.option_text: Only I follows (wrong: II is also a constructive action)
I and II follow (correct: skill development (I) improves employability; infrastructure projects (II) create direct jobs; penalising the unemployed (III) is counterproductive ✓)
Only III follows (wrong: penalising unemployed youth is not a solution)
All three follow (wrong: III punishes victims of unemployment)

questions.explanation: B is correct. (I) Vocational training = addresses skill gap (supply-side solution). (II) Infrastructure projects = creates employment (demand-side solution). (III) Penalising the unemployed = punishes people for a systemic problem; not a constructive course of action. I and II follow.

questions.stem:
Problem: Many children in a town are suffering from malnutrition.
Course of Action:
I. Mid-day meal programmes should be expanded in schools.
II. Awareness campaigns should educate parents about nutritious diets.
III. All children must eat at school canteens only.

options.option_text: Only I follows (wrong: II is also a valid complementary action)
I and II follow (correct: expanding meals (I) directly feeds children; awareness (II) addresses home nutrition; mandatory school eating (III) is impractical and intrusive ✓)
All three follow (wrong: III is extreme and impractical)
Only III follows (wrong: this alone doesn't solve malnutrition comprehensively)

questions.explanation: B is correct. (I) Mid-day meals = provides direct nutrition during school hours. (II) Parental awareness = addresses malnutrition at home too. (III) Mandatory school canteen eating = intrusive, impractical, doesn't address all children (especially non-school-goers). I and II follow.

questions.stem:
Problem: Cybercrime is increasing at an alarming rate in the country.
Course of Action:
I. The government should strengthen cyber laws and increase penalties.
II. Awareness campaigns should educate citizens about online safety.
III. All internet usage should be monitored 24×7.

options.option_text: Only I follows (wrong: II also addresses prevention)
Only III follows (wrong: mass surveillance is extreme and privacy-violating)
I and II follow (correct: stronger laws (I) deter criminals; awareness (II) protects potential victims; mass monitoring (III) violates privacy ✓)
All three follow (wrong: III raises serious civil liberties concerns)

questions.explanation: C is correct. (I) Stronger cyber laws = deters potential criminals. (II) Public awareness = protects citizens by educating them. (III) 24×7 internet monitoring of ALL users = mass surveillance; violates privacy rights and is technologically extreme. I and II are proportionate responses.

questions.stem:
Problem: Air quality in a major city has deteriorated to hazardous levels.
Course of Action:
I. The city should shift all industries to renewable energy and clean technology.
II. Odd-even number vehicle restrictions should be implemented.
III. Citizens should be compensated for reduced outdoor activities.

options.option_text: Only I follows (wrong: I is long-term; II is an immediate practical measure)
I and II follow (correct: industrial clean energy (I) addresses root cause; odd-even vehicles (II) reduces immediate pollution ✓; III doesn't reduce pollution)
Only III follows (wrong: compensation doesn't improve air quality)
All three follow (wrong: III is irrelevant to improving air quality)

questions.explanation: B is correct. (I) Shifting to clean energy = addresses root cause (industrial emissions). (II) Odd-even vehicle restriction = immediate practical measure to reduce vehicular pollution. (III) Compensating citizens = compensatory measure that doesn't address air quality itself — not a course of action that improves the situation. I and II follow.

questions.stem:
Problem: A hospital has been reporting a high number of preventable infections among patients.
Course of Action:
I. Strict hygiene and sterilisation protocols must be enforced immediately.
II. Training should be provided to all staff on infection control.
III. Infected patients should be discharged immediately to prevent spread.

options.option_text: Only I follows (wrong: II also addresses staff competence)
I and II follow (correct: hygiene protocols (I) address immediate cleanliness; staff training (II) addresses knowledge gap; discharging infected patients (III) is medically irresponsible ✓)
Only III follows (wrong: discharging sick patients can spread infection to the community)
All three follow (wrong: III could worsen public health by sending infected patients into the community)

questions.explanation: B is correct. (I) Strict hygiene = immediate preventive measure. (II) Staff training = addresses knowledge and behaviour causing infections. (III) Discharging infected patients = medically irresponsible; infected patients need treatment, not discharge; this could spread infection to the public. I and II follow.
